text:
incident-bot: 🔔 AUTO-PAGE fired for service=rlhf-inference-v2 (canary) — metric=5xx_rate p95 > 1.5% for 10m. Link: https://ops.redwood.example.com/alerts/3109876543

mika: ugh, I just kicked the canary rollout ~8m ago.

jamal: acked via pd-bot :white_check_mark: i'm taking first touch. what's the canary percent?

mika: canary = 8% traffic, rolling to eu-region nodes. nothing unusual in the deploy job logs.

jamal: checking traces and recent infra changes.

pd-bot: PagerDuty incident INC-2023109876 created and assigned to jamal. Escalation policy: eng-oncall -> sre -> platform.

tara: @jamal i'm on watch, pulling k8s events + node mem.

jamal: observability shows rlhf-inference-v2 canary pods hitting OOMKill spikes on two nodes, memory usage climbs ~10% higher post-release. p95 latency up too. dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood.example.com/d/rlhf_canary/overview

joel: rolling kernel/driver not touched in this release right? last infra change was yesterday for autoscaler.

mika: no infra changes in this rollout. only model binary + a small allocator tweak.

tara: looks like KV-cache key growth is higher for this model variant, might be leaking across requests. runbook: https://runbooks.redwood.example.com/rlhf-memory-leak

jamal: quick mitigation plan: 1) divert canary traffic back to stable 2) scale down canary pods 3) rollback release. anyone object?

mika: +1 to rollback. initiating now.

deploy-bot: rollback start: release=rlhf-inference-v2 commit=sha256:9a8b -> rolling back to rlhf-inference-v1, initiating traffic diversion.

jamal: diverting traffic via route-split -> set canary=0% using control-plane API:
```bash
redwoodctl rollout set -svc rlhf-inference -env prod -canary 0
```

tara: also cordon the two affected nodes and drain gracefully:
```bash
kubectl cordon node/eu-gpu-07
kubectl drain node/eu-gpu-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120
```

joel: scheduling extra capacity in eu-stage to take steady traffic while we stabilize. autoscaler alerted but we forced scale-up.

jamal: pd-bot: update — incident acknowledged, performing rollback and traffic diversion. notifying customers with potential impact.

mika: adding short blurb to status page draft: "We observed elevated 5xx for a canary release of rlhf-inference. Traffic was diverted and release rolled back. Some customers saw increased latency and sporadic 502s for ~12 minutes."

tara: after drain, I see memory pressure drop on remaining nodes. no more OOMKills in last 3m.

jamal: can we confirm no other regions affected?

joel: checked global metrics, only eu region spike. asia/na unaffected.

pd-bot: escalation suppressed (issue contained). next on-call rota: @tara at 23:00 UTC for handoff.

mika: extracting heap profiles from crashed pods and uploading: https://artifacts.redwood.example.com/rlhf/heapshots/3109876543

tara: saved core dump and started diff trace between v1 and v2 allocator paths. preliminary looks like a retained reference from kv-cache eviction not being triggered due to a config flag flip.

jamal: nice catch. was a config gate in model binary defaulting to cache_persist=true when it should be false for canary.

mika: I pushed a hotfix branch to revert gate and will run a small canary after approval.

joel: recommend adding a preflight memory smokecheck to the rollout pipeline to catch this class of regressions. filing ticket.

mika: ticket created: INFRA-1294 preflight-memory-smokechecks.

jamal: PD incident notes: root cause = model variant introduced aggressive KV persistence causing memory growth. mitigation = rollback + cordon/drain nodes + traffic diversion. customer impact = elevated latency and intermittent 502s for eu customers for ~12m.

tara: handing off to postmortem owners: @mika to lead RCA, @joel to own infra action, @jamal to own runbook update.

pd-bot: incident status -> resolved. incident duration: 00:14:17.

mika: thanks all. will schedule a short blameless postmortem and include the heap diff and rollout logs.

joel: follow-up ops task: add alert to detect unusual kv-cache growth by model-tag.

mika: pinging support to surface to any active customers impacted. support-ops notified.

support-ops (auto): acknowledged, creating customer outreach list.

jamal: closing thread — leave retention for 30d then archive. :wave:
